payload.text:
I wouldn't merge this yet. The dedupe doesn't work for the case the branch exists to handle.

**Blocker: `dedupe` compares objects instead of ids** (`src/dedupe.js`)
`[...new Set(contacts)]` only removes an entry if it's the exact same object in memory. When two imports overlap, the same contact comes in as two separate objects with the same id, so both are kept. The README says this outright: "Identity is the id, never object identity." I checked it: `mergeImports([{id:1,name:'A'}], [{id:1,name:'A'}])` returns both contacts. That means `mergeImports` currently just joins the lists together.

A fix that keeps the first contact seen for each id, as the README describes:
```js
function dedupe(contacts) {
  const seen = new Set();
  return contacts.filter((c) => !seen.has(c.id) && seen.add(c.id));
}
```

**The tests miss the bug** (`test/dedupe.test.js`)
- "the same object is not repeated" only checks one object listed twice, which `Set` already handles. Add a test with two separate objects that share an id, and check that the first one is the one kept.
- `mergeImports` has no test at all. Add one with two lists that overlap.

**Minor**
- `order.js` / `byName`: looks fine. It sorts a copy, so the input isn't changed, and the test checks that. Contacts with no name sort as `''`, which puts them first. That's fine if you meant it.
- The CHANGELOG entry, the version bump to 2.2.0 and the README sections all match what the code is meant to do. Once the dedupe fix is in, they'll be accurate.

I didn't change anything on the branch.
